analysis.investment_thesis: Affle is India's most compelling listed digital advertising play, with a 45% revenue and profit CAGR over 7 years, virtually zero debt, INR 1,047 Cr in cash, and consistently positive FCF — all signs of a high-quality business. The 47x P/E is demanding and the 14% ROE is disappointing for a technology company; I want to own more but need either a price correction or a step-up in ROE.
key_strengths: Revenue CAGR of 45.1% over 7 years (INR 167 Cr → INR 2,266 Cr) with net profit at 45.3% CAGR — rare consistency in Indian tech
Near-zero debt (D/E: 0.01), INR 1,047 Cr cash on balance sheet, and FCF positive every year — the balance sheet is pristine
India's digital advertising market is underpenetrated; smartphone and internet adoption curves give a genuine 10-year growth runway for Affle's CPCU (cost-per-converted-user) model
key_risks: ROE of 14% is mediocre for a tech company priced at 47x earnings — suggests either excessive goodwill from acquisitions or incomplete monetization of the platform
Aggressive inorganic growth (Appnext, Mediasmart, Jampp, RevX, YouAppi) creates integration risk and inflates the asset base without proportional earnings improvement
EV/EBITDA of 40.3x and P/S of 7.98x leave very little room for error; any demand softness in digital ad spending will punish the stock severely
red_flags: ROE declining or suppressed at 14% despite 45% growth — points to large goodwill/intangibles on balance sheet diluting return ratios; total assets rose from INR 402 Cr (FY20) to INR 3,914 Cr (FY25) while equity grew proportionally less efficiently
Gross margin of only 29% suggests significant traffic acquisition costs — competitive pressure in programmatic advertising globally could squeeze margins further
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Affle is the rare Indian tech company that has built a genuinely global mobile advertising platform through a combination of organic growth and disciplined acquisitions. The 45% revenue CAGR, zero-debt balance sheet, and consistently positive FCF (INR 266 Cr in FY25) tick many boxes for me. The promoter at 54.92% is adequately invested, and digital advertising in India — driven by UPI, e-commerce, gaming, and OTT — is still in early innings. The CPCU model is differentiated and measurable for advertisers, which gives it pricing power.

My hesitation is purely valuation and ROE. Paying 47x earnings for a business generating 14% ROE is not value investing — it is a bet purely on growth continuation. If Affle can improve its ROE to 20%+ (either by monetizing its acquisition portfolio better or by letting cash-generating operations scale), this deserves a premium rating. But at current prices, I am comfortable holding but not aggressively adding. A correction to 30–35x P/E or evidence of ROE expansion would make this a genuine high-conviction position.
